title: Dashboard bug follow-up pocket log
content:
Quick pocket log for dashboard issues + follow-ups (running notes). Not a polished postmortem — just my brain dump while juggling Slack + alerts.

Context:
- Intermittent missing-series on /console/per-route-latency for several customer routes (noticed 2026-03-09 09:15 PST).
- Affected customers: AcmePay (prod-us), QuillAnalytics (prod-eu). Both reported timeouts in app telemetry then opened support tickets.
- Symptoms: frontend shows blank chart tiles (no series) for last-1h; metric ingestion still visible in raw metrics store for same timeframe.
- Hypothesis: query-layer caching or dashboard query aggregation failing when series cardinality above threshold. Could also be front-end transform crash (NPE) when series list is empty.

Immediate triage steps (done):
- 09:20: check metrics source (prom/ingest): ingestion pipeline healthy, no backfill. (Samir)
- 09:30: verified raw series present using metrics-explorer: route=route-X had 1800 series for last 1h — OK.
- 09:40: reproduced in staging by sending high-cardinality request set — dashboards returned empty tiles.
- 09:50: rolled back console frontend commit fd3b9 -> candidate cause? No change.
- 10:10: toggled 'compact-aggregation' flag on query service to false -> dashboards returned series again in staging.

Interim workaround (applied to prod-us at 10:45):
- Flip feature flag kv: console-query/compact-aggregation = false for prod-us region. Immediate customer impact: dashboards restored for AcmePay. Need to monitor for cost increase (query volume up ~12%).

Open action items (prioritized):
- [P0] (Rory) Add guard in query-service to handle >1024 series without dropping them silently. Simple fix: return empty placeholder + log instead of throwing -> estimate 3-4h.
- [P0] (Aisha) Run canary for kb truncation safety in Prod-EU tomorrow 03/11 09:00 UTC.
- [P1] (Samir) Add dashboard test sim that feeds high-cardinality series to catch regression in CI. -> ticket OBS-1012.
- [P2] (Maya) Write brief customer note for AcmePay w/ explanation + ETA for permanent fix. Draft in support ticket.

Questions to resolve:
- Why did compact-aggregation flag cause empty tiles instead of fallback behavior? Where is the implicit exception raised? stack traces point to console-query v2 line 188 (transform.js) but staging logs are noisy.
- Is there a rate/timeout threshold where the frontend will momentarily show empty tiles while the backend streams partial results? Need to instrument stream-start and tile-render times.

Notes / debug snippets:
- Quick grep of prod logs: "TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined" at transform.js:188 -> points to reducer assuming series array exists.
- Query service shard logs show spikes of 503 at 09:12-09:18 — correlates with customer errors. Root cause likely upstream aggregator returning null payload when cardinality > 2048.
- Tooling: use metrics-flame and kibana-query with timeframe +/- 5m around incidents.

Temporary monitoring checks (add to obs dashboard):
- Tile: count(null_payloads) by aggregator_cluster (alert if > 5 in 5m)
- Tile: query_latency_95 per region (alert if > 1200ms)
- Tile: feature_flag_changes (to detect accidental flips)

Draft PR plan:
- Small change in console-query: add safe-guard before transform, return empty series list + log event {tag: 'safe-empty-series'}. Then: add unit tests for zero/undefined series, e2e with canned high-cardinality dataset.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4213 (WIP) — needs review from @Samir and @Aisha.

Support comms / Slack references:
- Notified #obs-triage at 10:05 — pinned logs.
- Support ticket for AcmePay INC-5542 (linked in Jira OBS-987).
- Customer workaround: ask them to reduce rolling-window cardinality for any ad-hoc queries we suspect trigger issue (temporary).

Follow-ups after deploy:
- Monitor cost impact of disabling compact-aggregation for 48h; rollback if query costs grow >20% month-to-date forecast.
- Run through runbook checklist: postmortem stub + RCA owner (tentatively: Rory).
- Add a small regression test to nightly canary suite that runs dashboard render with synthetic 2500 series.

Random notes to self:
- Check if dedicated instances for query aggregator have new kernel/driver versions (might affect memory behavior).
- Circle back with infra to see if autoscaler trimmed aggregator nodes around 09:10 — could have reduced capacity causing upstream null responses.

End-of-day quick summary (to paste into incident thread):
- What: Empty dashboard tiles for high-cardinality routes -> caused by compact-aggregation path failing on large series sets.
- Mitigation: toggled compact-aggregation=false in prod-us -> dashboards restored.
- Next steps: safe-guard in query-service + canary + customer comms.

TODO (personal):
- Push small PR w/ guard and tests (today EOD).
- Draft customer note for AcmePay (send tomorrow morning).
- Add the three monitoring tiles to team dashboard (Aisha to own).
__note: This file intentionally informal — personal triage scratchpad saved to Drive for quick recall and handoff.
